summary: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT): 26 reviewed current record claims in scoped correction v6-audit-fix-20261014. Unit, course, publisher and data-use conditions remain distinct; recorded gaps and held historical material are preserved.

claimChanges.claimText: MIT does not permit Medium Risk data in publicly available GenAI tools. High Risk MIT information must not be used with any GenAI tool, including MIT enterprise tools; report an existing high-risk disclosure to security@mit.edu immediately. Public tools are not recommended for Low Risk MIT data.

MIT guidance requires GenAI use to comply with applicable law, Institute policies, Information Protection guidelines, WISP, and applicable DLCI policies. The linked IS&T page still mentions EO 14110; that revoked order is not presented here as a current legal obligation.
Adobe Firefly is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
AWS Bedrock is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
AWS Sagemaker is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Azure OpenAI is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Open AI ChatGPT is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.

Google Gemini is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free with an MIT Google Workspace account. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Google Vertex is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Microsoft Copilot is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, students, and affiliates. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.

Microsoft Copilot for M365 is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.

Google NotebookLM is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free with an MIT Google Workspace account. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Salesforce Einstein is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Parley is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Zoom AI Companion is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, students, and affiliates. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.

MIT Libraries advises citing or acknowledging AI contributions in academic papers and consulting the applicable school, class, and publication policies. This is citation guidance, not a universal assessment-use permission or a new university-wide mandatory disclosure rule.
Purchasing new GenAI tools at MIT requires the VPF procurement process. For a tool not on IS&T's list, request an assessment from ai-guidance@mit.edu before use or purchase.
MIT Libraries states that authors are responsible for their work and advises verifying information provided by generative AI. Scope: academic and research writing guidance.

IS&T lists MIT-licensed GenAI tools approved for low- and medium-risk information. Tools not listed require an assessment before use or purchase; no GenAI tool is approved for High Risk MIT information. Tool access does not authorize coursework or exam use.

For Fall 2026, MIT faculty guidance states that there are no Institute-wide requirements for setting classroom AI-use policies. Instructors are encouraged to publish clear course policies; sample policy menus are not adopted rules for every course.

MIT's August 13, 2026 committee report states that COD does not consider AI-detector output alone sufficient for an AI-related academic integrity case. This records the committee's description of COD practice, not a blanket detector ban.
MIT TLL strongly recommends against using AI-detection tools. This is teaching guidance, not a university-wide statutory prohibition.

MIT's August 2026 committee report recommends AI-use statements in all theses and says AI should not be listed as a co-author. Researchers should also check journal and conference requirements. This is a committee recommendation; a new mandatory thesis rule has not been established by this source.

For applicable AI human-subjects research applications, COUHES guidance requires available Data Cards and adequate consent transparency. Model Cards are recommended when developing or further developing a model; this does not apply to all coursework.

Students needing disability accommodations to participate in a COD process are directed to Disability and Access Services. This is a general disciplinary procedure resource, not an AI-specific sanction.

Permission to return to MIT after suspension does not guarantee return to the same department, degree program, lab group, or related position. This is a general COD sanction condition, not an AI-specific penalty.

claimChanges.claimText: MIT does not permit Medium Risk data in publicly available GenAI tools. High Risk MIT information must not be used with any GenAI tool, including MIT enterprise tools; report an existing high-risk disclosure to security@mit.edu immediately. Public tools are not recommended for Low Risk MIT data.

MIT guidance requires GenAI use to comply with applicable law, Institute policies, Information Protection guidelines, WISP, and applicable DLCI policies. The linked IS&T page still mentions EO 14110; that revoked order is not presented here as a current legal obligation.
Adobe Firefly is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
AWS Bedrock is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
AWS Sagemaker is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Azure OpenAI is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Open AI ChatGPT is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.

Google Gemini is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free with an MIT Google Workspace account. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Google Vertex is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Microsoft Copilot is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, students, and affiliates. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.

Microsoft Copilot for M365 is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.

Google NotebookLM is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free with an MIT Google Workspace account. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Salesforce Einstein is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Parley is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Zoom AI Companion is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, students, and affiliates. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.

MIT Libraries advises citing or acknowledging AI contributions in academic papers and consulting the applicable school, class, and publication policies. This is citation guidance, not a universal assessment-use permission or a new university-wide mandatory disclosure rule.
Purchasing new GenAI tools at MIT requires the VPF procurement process. For a tool not on IS&T's list, request an assessment from ai-guidance@mit.edu before use or purchase.
MIT Libraries states that authors are responsible for their work and advises verifying information provided by generative AI. Scope: academic and research writing guidance.

IS&T lists MIT-licensed GenAI tools approved for low- and medium-risk information. Tools not listed require an assessment before use or purchase; no GenAI tool is approved for High Risk MIT information. Tool access does not authorize coursework or exam use.

Historical IS&T guidance captured on May 6, 2026: MIT prohibits the use of generative AI for purposes that may require in-depth risk assessments without prior consultation with ai-guidance@mit.edu. Such purposes include recruitment and hiring of employees, evaluating student academic performance, making investment decisions, and complaint and dispute resolution. This specific provision is not reproduced on the current guidance page; its current applicability has not been confirmed.

Historical IS&T guidance captured on May 6, 2026: MIT departments, labs, centers, and institutes (DLCIs) already using a generative AI tool or service must ensure that the tool complies with all Institute policies and Information Protection guidelines, and must contact ai-guidance@mit.edu for consultation or assessment if needed. This specific provision is not reproduced on the current guidance page; its current applicability has not been confirmed.

For Fall 2026, MIT faculty guidance states that there are no Institute-wide requirements for setting classroom AI-use policies. Instructors are encouraged to publish clear course policies; sample policy menus are not adopted rules for every course.

MIT's August 13, 2026 committee report states that COD does not consider AI-detector output alone sufficient for an AI-related academic integrity case. This records the committee's description of COD practice, not a blanket detector ban.
MIT TLL strongly recommends against using AI-detection tools. This is teaching guidance, not a university-wide statutory prohibition.

MIT's August 2026 committee report recommends AI-use statements in all theses and says AI should not be listed as a co-author. Researchers should also check journal and conference requirements. This is a committee recommendation; a new mandatory thesis rule has not been established by this source.

For applicable AI human-subjects research applications, COUHES guidance requires available Data Cards and adequate consent transparency. Model Cards are recommended when developing or further developing a model; this does not apply to all coursework.

Students needing disability accommodations to participate in a COD process are directed to Disability and Access Services. This is a general disciplinary procedure resource, not an AI-specific sanction.

Permission to return to MIT after suspension does not guarantee return to the same department, degree program, lab group, or related position. This is a general COD sanction condition, not an AI-specific penalty.

claimChanges.claimText: MIT does not permit Medium Risk data in publicly available GenAI tools. High Risk MIT information must not be used with any GenAI tool, including MIT enterprise tools; report an existing high-risk disclosure to security@mit.edu immediately. Public tools are not recommended for Low Risk MIT data.

MIT guidance requires GenAI use to comply with applicable law, Institute policies, Information Protection guidelines, WISP, and applicable DLCI policies. The linked IS&T page still mentions EO 14110; that revoked order is not presented here as a current legal obligation.
Adobe Firefly is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
AWS Bedrock is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
AWS Sagemaker is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Azure OpenAI is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Open AI ChatGPT is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.

Google Gemini is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free with an MIT Google Workspace account. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Google Vertex is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Microsoft Copilot is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, students, and affiliates. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.

Microsoft Copilot for M365 is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.

Google NotebookLM is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free with an MIT Google Workspace account. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Salesforce Einstein is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Parley is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Zoom AI Companion is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, students, and affiliates. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.

MIT Libraries advises citing or acknowledging AI contributions in academic papers and consulting the applicable school, class, and publication policies. This is citation guidance, not a universal assessment-use permission or a new university-wide mandatory disclosure rule.
Purchasing new GenAI tools at MIT requires the VPF procurement process. For a tool not on IS&T's list, request an assessment from ai-guidance@mit.edu before use or purchase.
MIT Libraries states that authors are responsible for their work and advises verifying information provided by generative AI. Scope: academic and research writing guidance.

IS&T lists MIT-licensed GenAI tools approved for low- and medium-risk information. Tools not listed require an assessment before use or purchase; no GenAI tool is approved for High Risk MIT information. Tool access does not authorize coursework or exam use.

Historical IS&T guidance captured on May 6, 2026: MIT prohibits the use of generative AI for purposes that may require in-depth risk assessments without prior consultation with ai-guidance@mit.edu. Such purposes include recruitment and hiring of employees, evaluating student academic performance, making investment decisions, and complaint and dispute resolution. This specific provision is not reproduced on the current guidance page; its current applicability has not been confirmed.

Historical IS&T guidance captured on May 6, 2026: MIT departments, labs, centers, and institutes (DLCIs) already using a generative AI tool or service must ensure that the tool complies with all Institute policies and Information Protection guidelines, and must contact ai-guidance@mit.edu for consultation or assessment if needed. This specific provision is not reproduced on the current guidance page; its current applicability has not been confirmed.

For Fall 2026, MIT faculty guidance states that there are no Institute-wide requirements for setting classroom AI-use policies. Instructors are encouraged to publish clear course policies; sample policy menus are not adopted rules for every course.

MIT's August 13, 2026 committee report states that COD does not consider AI-detector output alone sufficient for an AI-related academic integrity case. This records the committee's description of COD practice, not a blanket detector ban.
MIT TLL strongly recommends against using AI-detection tools. This is teaching guidance, not a university-wide statutory prohibition.

MIT's August 2026 committee report recommends AI-use statements in all theses and says AI should not be listed as a co-author. Researchers should also check journal and conference requirements. This is a committee recommendation; a new mandatory thesis rule has not been established by this source.

For applicable AI human-subjects research applications, COUHES guidance requires available Data Cards and adequate consent transparency. Model Cards are recommended when developing or further developing a model; this does not apply to all coursework.

Students needing disability accommodations to participate in a COD process are directed to Disability and Access Services. This is a general disciplinary procedure resource, not an AI-specific sanction.

Permission to return to MIT after suspension does not guarantee return to the same department, degree program, lab group, or related position. This is a general COD sanction condition, not an AI-specific penalty.

claimChanges.claimText: MIT does not permit Medium Risk data in publicly available GenAI tools. High Risk MIT information must not be used with any GenAI tool, including MIT enterprise tools; report an existing high-risk disclosure to security@mit.edu immediately. Public tools are not recommended for Low Risk MIT data.

MIT guidance requires GenAI use to comply with applicable law, Institute policies, Information Protection guidelines, WISP, and applicable DLCI policies. The linked IS&T page still mentions EO 14110; that revoked order is not presented here as a current legal obligation.
Adobe Firefly is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
AWS Bedrock is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
AWS Sagemaker is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Azure OpenAI is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Open AI ChatGPT is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.

Google Gemini is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free with an MIT Google Workspace account. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Google Vertex is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Microsoft Copilot is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, students, and affiliates. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.

Microsoft Copilot for M365 is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.

Google NotebookLM is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free with an MIT Google Workspace account. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Salesforce Einstein is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty and staff. Cost: Institute cost object required. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Parley is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, and students. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.
Zoom AI Companion is listed by MIT IS&T for MIT faculty, staff, students, and affiliates. Cost: Free. Institutional access and data restrictions do not establish assessment permission.

MIT Libraries advises citing or acknowledging AI contributions in academic papers and consulting the applicable school, class, and publication policies. This is citation guidance, not a universal assessment-use permission or a new university-wide mandatory disclosure rule.
Purchasing new GenAI tools at MIT requires the VPF procurement process. For a tool not on IS&T's list, request an assessment from ai-guidance@mit.edu before use or purchase.
MIT Libraries states that authors are responsible for their work and advises verifying information provided by generative AI. Scope: academic and research writing guidance.

IS&T lists MIT-licensed GenAI tools approved for low- and medium-risk information. Tools not listed require an assessment before use or purchase; no GenAI tool is approved for High Risk MIT information. Tool access does not authorize coursework or exam use.

Historical IS&T guidance captured on May 6, 2026: MIT prohibits the use of generative AI for purposes that may require in-depth risk assessments without prior consultation with ai-guidance@mit.edu. Such purposes include recruitment and hiring of employees, evaluating student academic performance, making investment decisions, and complaint and dispute resolution. This specific provision is not reproduced on the current guidance page; its current applicability has not been confirmed.

Historical IS&T guidance captured on May 6, 2026: MIT departments, labs, centers, and institutes (DLCIs) already using a generative AI tool or service must ensure that the tool complies with all Institute policies and Information Protection guidelines, and must contact ai-guidance@mit.edu for consultation or assessment if needed. This specific provision is not reproduced on the current guidance page; its current applicability has not been confirmed.

For Fall 2026, MIT faculty guidance states that there are no Institute-wide requirements for setting classroom AI-use policies. Instructors are encouraged to publish clear course policies; sample policy menus are not adopted rules for every course.

MIT's August 13, 2026 committee report states that COD does not consider AI-detector output alone sufficient for an AI-related academic integrity case. This records the committee's description of COD practice, not a blanket detector ban.
MIT TLL strongly recommends against using AI-detection tools. This is teaching guidance, not a university-wide statutory prohibition.

MIT's August 2026 committee report recommends AI-use statements in all theses and says AI should not be listed as a co-author. Researchers should also check journal and conference requirements. This is a committee recommendation; a new mandatory thesis rule has not been established by this source.

For applicable AI human-subjects research applications, COUHES guidance requires available Data Cards and adequate consent transparency. Model Cards are recommended when developing or further developing a model; this does not apply to all coursework.

Students needing disability accommodations to participate in a COD process are directed to Disability and Access Services. This is a general disciplinary procedure resource, not an AI-specific sanction.

Permission to return to MIT after suspension does not guarantee return to the same department, degree program, lab group, or related position. This is a general COD sanction condition, not an AI-specific penalty.
